newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen up after Q4 ECI.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen up after Q4 ECI.

text.p: U.S. stocks are seen opening higher on Tuesday after the fourth-quarter employment cost index came in lower than expected, analysts said.
PETER CARDILLO, DIRECTOR OF RESEARCH AT WESTFALIA INVESTEMENTS:

-- "It's basically what the Street was expecting. We came in less that one percent and that's good. Bonds are strong so the (stock) market will have a strong opening. I think we'll stablize today and move higher."

-- The data tell us that we have had higher wages. That shouldn't scare anyone. It shows the economy is moving ahead. Inflation is not getting out of hand and does not pose a threat of accelerating. That is the key."

The fourth quarter ECI rose 0.8 percent, after rising 0.6 percent in the third quarter, the Labor Department said. Economists polled by Reuters estimated, on average, that the ECI would rise 0.9 percent in the fourth quarter.
The index gauges not only the cost of workers' wages but also the cost of their benefits.
PHIL ORLANDO, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER OF VALUE LINE'S ASSET MANAGEMENT DIVISION:
-- "It's a good number...The concern going into this number was that it was going to be north of one percent, that's why we saw the bond approaching seven percent over the last couple days."

-- "Stocks will probably rally on this....We've lost some 300 points in the Dow over the last three or four days, so I think we may have touched bottom with that 6600 level intraday yesterday and we may trade higher on this."
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond surged 1-7/32 to yield 6.84 percent in reaction to the ECI data.
THOM BROWN, MANAGING DIRECTOR OF RUTHERFORD BROWN AND CATHERWOOD:

-- The ECI data "will rally the (stock) market because the market yesterday was under weight of higher bond yields. The data has caused a strong bond rally and that will give stocks a boost. Stocks tried to rally a few times yesterday but could not do it in the face of deterioration in the bond market."
